rows.question: What kind of engineer is Jared?

baseline.answer: Jared is a backend-to-full-stack engineer who used code review and senior guidance before independently implementing an MVP React frontend with documentation and targeted help. At Dogly, he later retained migrations and routing while the frontend engineer implemented bounded controller actions, and his later work became highly autonomous. He pushed back on broader React use for relatively static authentication pages, citing Rails’ existing secure handling, limited SEO partly due to insufficient server-side rendering, downstream migration work, and revenue-generating roadmap priorities; he documented dependencies and time cost while acknowledging the consistency benefit. He has direct professional engineer-to-engineer collaboration experience, while sustained larger-team engineering experience remains new context.

rows.question: What are some examples of product decisions Jared has influenced, not just engineering work he's implemented?

rows.question: Tell me more about the first example. What did Jared have to convince people of?

baseline.answer: During the F Street Anthropologie opening, Jared had to convince stakeholders of the potential of a comparatively green manager he hired. He recognized her strong skills in People, Product, Process thinking, and aesthetic vision. To support her development, he partnered with her manager, provided her exposure to higher-level meetings, and maintained a supportive guide posture. Her manager became Assistant Store Manager after roughly six months, and the lower-level manager then moved into that role and developed her own replacement behind her.
